findings.title: cites_round's docstring omits the legitimate 'carried' closure channel
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:182-192: "every id of its last tally closed through `honored`, `adjudicated`, `rescan` or `seeded`"
src/CLI/Release.jl:201-202: `get(e, "closed_by", nothing) in ("honored", "adjudicated", "rescan", "seeded") || String(id) in carried`
findings.description: The docstring of `cites_round` (which gates whether a release may cite a /check-docs round) lists four closure channels, but the code accepts a fifth disjunctive path: an id carried into the next round (RULE.INST.CARRY), read from ROUND.toml's `closed_by.carried`. A reader of only the docstring would wrongly conclude a carried finding blocks release-citation.
findings.resolution_hint: Add 'or was carried into the next round (closed_by.carried)' to the docstring's closure-channel list.

findings.title: pass_scope's docstring omits the unconditional-suspect branch for location-less findings
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:235-237: "plus any id that pass closed whose named locations the fix pass has touched again"
src/CLI/Passes.jl:256-259: `(isempty(named) || any(x -> x in touched, named)) && push!(suspects, id)`
findings.description: The docstring says a closed finding becomes a suspect only when the fix pass touched its named files. The code's condition is an OR: a closed finding with NO named locations is unconditionally re-suspected every later pass, a nuance recorded only in an inline body comment, not in the docstring itself.
findings.resolution_hint: State the location-less case explicitly in the docstring alongside the touched-file case.

findings.title: the top-level module map's 'The engines:' list omits Consolidate, paired with HtmlWalker everywhere else
locations: src/GBGCodingTools.jl:34-42: "`HtmlWalker` — the Gumbo walker shared by the consolidator and the built-HTML scans."
findings.description: CLAUDE.md names Consolidate.jl an engine alongside HtmlWalker, and HtmlWalker's own docstring calls itself 'shared by the consolidator'. Yet GBGCodingTools.jl's module map, which lists TestHarness/Reflection/Witnesses, the scan engine, TreeHash and HtmlWalker as 'The engines', never mentions Consolidate.jl / `consolidate`, despite it being used directly by Rounds.jl and Passes.jl.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a bullet for `consolidate` beside HtmlWalker in the 'The engines:' list.

findings.title: usage() text misstates what CLI exit code 2 means
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:108: "usage: gbg [--dev] <noun> [<verb>] [options]   (exit 0 clean · 1 finding · 2 a second finding · 3 crash)"
findings.description: The printed usage banner says exit 2 means 'a second finding'. Every other statement of the contract — main's own docstring twelve lines above ('2 cannot evaluate'), the module docstring, and ARCHITECTURE — says exit 2 means cannot evaluate. The banner a user sees at the terminal contradicts the documented and implemented contract.
findings.resolution_hint: Change '2 a second finding' to '2 cannot evaluate' to match main's own docstring.
